PullRequest.Title: editor: align Connected cap contour with the control radius
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #340635. Related work: #340822, #340823, and #336898.

An active Connected editor tab can look sharper than its freestanding Pill neighbors because its outline reduces the visible inner curve. Derive the editor cap's outer radius from the existing control radius plus the existing stroke thickness, instead of introducing a new radius token.

The change is editor-scoped. Upper-row/inactive pills, shoulders, hit targets, layout, and generic chat-tab geometry stay unchanged. Existing regression expectations follow the adjusted outer cap, including clipped painting and border continuity.

When the outline matches the fill or is transparent, the larger outer silhouette is visible instead of the smaller outlined inner contour. This tradeoff was inspected with actual native color customizations and accepted.

## Testing

1. Use Connected editor tabs and select first, middle, and terminal tabs. Compare the active cap with freestanding neighbors.
2. Repeat with default and compact tab heights, wrapped rows, and separate pinned rows. Upper pills and shoulder joins should remain unchanged.
3. Check both high-contrast themes, multi-selection, keyboard-focused Close actions, and horizontally clipped active tabs.
4. Set `modernEditorTab.activeBackground` to `#FDE68A` through `workbench.colorCustomizations`. Set both `tab.border` and `editorGroupHeader.tabsBorder` to `#7C3AED`, then `#FDE68A`, then `#00000000`. Compare the outlined inner contour with the same-fill/transparent outer silhouette.
5. Switch to Pill and Legacy styles. Their geometry should remain unchanged.

Local validation:
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/editorPart.test.ts` — passed.
- `npm test -- editorTabBar.spec.ts --workers=1` from `test/componentFixtures/playwright` — passed, including customized border continuity and disabled-hover high-contrast cases.
- Targeted ESLint and Stylelint — passed.
- Component Explorer before/after comparisons and native Code OSS customizations — passed. The pinned combined candidate preserves the approved editor and chat reference images.

## Visual evidence

The component comparison shows the original cap, adjusted cap, Pill reference, and hidden-stroke variants at matched scales. The native matrix shows the candidate in Monokai at normal zoom with default, contrasting, same-fill, and transparent borders.

![Matched component corners: original Connected, candidate, Pill, and hidden-stroke variants](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca373a75-6c46-4b33-ba56-818c8298e681)

![Native Monokai candidate: default, contrasting, same-fill, and transparent borders at normal zoom](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0bab804c-cae1-451e-9b85-a8284dd49407)

Final readiness gates are complete: native visual/customization approval, both local reviews, current-head Copilot review with no open findings, remote CI, and the exact-final cross-workstream validation passed. The corrected-identity signed head preserves the validated source tree. Collaborator approval remains a separate merge requirement.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render, select, wrap, and horizontally scroll Connected editor tabs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The browser already resolves the scoped tab CSS, lays out existing tab and overflow-edge elements, and paints their borders. The changed custom property replaces a 4px token with a calc resolving to 5px for the active lower-row cap; it adds no JavaScript, DOM access, selector, element, or synchronous layout read to this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible editor groups and tabs, including wrapped rows and clipped active tabs. Work remains proportional to the same number of styled elements; the diff does not increase effective cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI style/layout/paint remains serialized on the renderer main thread as before. No task, queue, limiter, IPC, or concurrent work is added or changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved. Browser style sharing/invalidation sees the same selector and declaration graph; only the computed length differs. Warm and cold rendering use the same existing stylesheet path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: all production diff content is one custom-property value, and every consumer is an existing border-radius or absolute overlay width on the same tab elements.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact rasterization cost is not measured, but the painted topology and element count are unchanged and the radius increases by one CSS pixel, so there is no scaling mechanism suggesting a meaningful regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing style/layout/paint work remains unchanged in count and scheduling; only the active cap contour dimensions change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply theme or size customizations while Connected editor tabs are visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A theme/size variable update already triggers browser style invalidation and repaint. The cap now also depends on the existing strokeThickness variable, so its computed radius updates during that same invalidation; no additional event handler or forced layout is introduced.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible active Connected tab caps across editor groups. The same existing style invalidation reaches those elements; no per-tab application callback is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing renderer style recalculation remains main-thread work with no new parallelism, fan-out, or queued tasks.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Theme CSS custom properties are resolved by the browser; there is no repository cache, miss retry, or retained key set affected by this change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the dependency changes computed paint geometry, and high confidence that no boundary or repeated-work mechanism is added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Customization frequency varies, but these updates are user-driven and infrequent. The changed dependency can repaint existing caps during a stroke-thickness update, without adding elements or repeated reads.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra arithmetic is a constant-time CSS calc within an already-required style update and does not create meaningful latency or rendering amplification.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run editor-tab unit, sessions, and component fixture tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Changed tests only update expected radius literals and an existing conditional expected value; they do not add test cases, loops, browser operations, screenshots, filesystem access, or waits.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing test matrix cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Test-runner concurrency and sequencing are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No test cache behavior is changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete test-file diffs.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the diff shows only expectation substitutions inside existing test execution.
Scenarios.Verdict: No test throughput or resource regression is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full four-file diff. The sole production change adjusts one scoped CSS radius expression; test changes update existing expectations. Tracing all consumers found no new DOM nodes, selectors, synchronous geometry reads, repeated work, retained state, concurrency, or subprocess/IPC/filesystem/database/network boundaries, so no finding was submitted.
